pure-announcement.rationale: This is threat-landscape analysis with remediation guidance built on the March 2026 incident cluster, not a product launch or release note, despite Tenable product pitches in the closing sections.

duplicate.rationale: siem-agentic-visibility-gap covers SIEMs' semantic blind spot for agent interactions, while this argues EDR's structural blind spot for ephemeral CI/CD credential theft and a preemptive exposure-management remedy — a reader of the existing concept learns the credential-economy framing, the actor division of labor, and the token-lifecycle countermeasures only here.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The incident spine is externally sourced — Microsoft and Google attribution of the Axios npm compromise, SANS analysis of TeamPCP, news coverage of the Claude source leak — so only the vendor's own unpublished telemetry framing is uncheckable.

durability.rationale: The structural arguments age well independent of the 2026 incidents: execution-layer detection cannot see ephemeral CI/CD build environments, exfiltrate-and-self-destruct malware outruns human triage, long-lived tokens are the enabling exposure, and short-lived OIDC-based automation removes it.

actionability.rationale: It prescribes concrete, product-agnostic steps a team can take this week — audit lockfiles, disable npm lifecycle hooks with --ignore-scripts, and replace long-lived CI/CD tokens with short-lived OIDC-based credentials.

atomicity.rationale: The note is one causal argument statable in a paragraph: supply chain attacks now industrialize theft of privileged developer credentials from CI/CD environments EDR cannot see, so defense must shift from execution-layer detection to preemptively eliminating the exposure conditions.
